name: Kiwi before bed

card.summary: Eating kiwifruit in the evening is proposed as a food-based sleep aid; the encyclopedic sources reviewed offer little on it.
card.note: Kiwifruit allergy exists and ranges from oral itching to anaphylaxis.

quick.overview:
The practice is eating kiwifruit shortly before bed in the hope of better sleep, which adherents link to appearance through skin and recovery.

Wikipedia's kiwifruit article covers nutrition and allergy but does not discuss sleep.
quick.mechanism: Kiwifruit is rich in vitamin C and vitamin K and contains carotenoids and fibre [1]. A sleep mechanism is not described in the source consulted.
quick.risks: Kiwifruit allergy, first described in 1981, ranges from oral allergy symptoms to anaphylaxis; the enzyme actinidain is an allergen for some people [1].

lead: Eating kiwifruit before bed is a food-based practice that some people adopt for sleep. Wikipedia's kiwifruit article describes the fruit as about 83% water, rich in vitamin C and vitamin K, and notes allergy risk, but does not discuss sleep effects [1].
Published trials of kiwifruit and self-reported sleep are small, and no appearance outcomes have been studied.

paras: Kiwifruit allergy was first described in 1981 and ranges from localised oral allergy syndrome to life-threatening anaphylaxis; wheezing is the most common severe symptom [1].
No studies found in the sources reviewed for this article.
